title: Development of an Educational Chatbot System for Enhancing Students’ Biology Learning Performance
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem that junior high school students often have limited time and support to learn and review biology outside class. The authors argue that traditional classroom instruction leaves students with insufficient opportunities to ask questions and to receive immediate feedback, which can reduce learning achievement, especially for students who begin with weaker prior knowledge.

To address this, the study developed an educational chatbot for biology learning using the LINE messaging platform. The chatbot provided learning videos, a biology assistant for answering concept questions, multiple-choice exercises with instant feedback, and a learning-record function that let students review their own activity logs. The content was based on Junyi Academy secondary biology materials, and the system was intended for out-of-class use.

The study used a quasi-experimental design in a grade 7 junior high school biology course in Taiwan. Thirty-four students were split into a control group that used a LINE discussion group outside class and an experimental group that used the biology chatbot; both groups received traditional classroom instruction from the teacher. Results showed that the chatbot group achieved significantly better post-test performance overall, with especially strong benefits for students with low prior knowledge. The paper concludes that the chatbot was effective for supporting biology learning outside class and suggests integrating AI and natural language processing in future versions.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental study with a control group, pretest covariate adjustment, and subgroup analyses, which provides moderate credibility. However, it is not randomized and the sample size is small, so there are important internal validity and generalizability concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The main achievement effect is large (η2=0.244), and the low-prior-knowledge subgroup effect is also large (η2=0.301). Although the study is small, the observed impact on a priority K-12 population is substantial.

interventions.use_case: LINE-based educational chatbot for grade 7 biology out-of-class support, including learning videos, concept Q&A, multiple-choice exercises, and learning-record review.

finding.finding_summary: The quasi-experimental study with n=34 grade 7 students found that the biology learning chatbot improved post-test learning achievement relative to a LINE discussion-group control. ANCOVA controlling for prior knowledge showed a significant advantage for the chatbot group (F(1,31)=9.821, p=0.004, η2=0.244), indicating a large effect.
finding.measure: Biology learning achievement post-test (paper-and-pencil test, out of 100), ANCOVA-adjusted comparison controlling for prior knowledge

finding.finding_summary: For students with low prior knowledge, the chatbot produced significantly higher adjusted biology achievement than the discussion-group control. The low-prior-knowledge subgroup analysis reported F(1,15)=8.999, p=0.009, η2=0.301, a large effect favoring the chatbot.
finding.measure: Biology learning achievement post-test among low prior knowledge students
finding.study_size: n=18 (low prior knowledge subgroup: 9 chatbot, 9 control)

finding.finding_summary: For students with high prior knowledge, the chatbot did not significantly outperform the discussion-group control on biology achievement. The ANCOVA found F(1,13)=1.412, p=0.256, η2=0.022, indicating a negligible difference between conditions.
finding.measure: Biology learning achievement post-test among high prior knowledge students
finding.study_size: n=16 (high prior knowledge subgroup: 8 chatbot, 8 control)
